solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some stick acting make-up on part of body

parts.note: A is a dictionary abbreviation for acting, as in a temporary title
slap is theatrical slang for stage make-up
taken as written
the wrist is a part of the body, article included

explanation.surface: Some sort of stick-on make-up for actors, applied to a part of the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acting make-up' reads as one phrase, but 'acting' gives A on its own and 'make-up' gives SLAP, the theatre word for greasepaint.
explanation.definitionFit: To get some stick is to be criticised; a mild token rebuke is the idiom for exactly that.

clue.text: Genuine claims upset boss, the first to pay compensation

indicators.note: claims is read as holds or takes in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: genuine means real

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read the letters backwards

parts.note: sir is a form of address for a boss or master

indicators.note: the first to picks out the opening letter of the following word, pay

explanation.surface: Someone with real grievances turns on the boss and demands payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' is a reversal in a down clue, turning the boss plus P; 'claims' means holds. SIR is the respectful word for a boss or master.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprisal in an older sense means a payment or seizure made by way of redress, a form of indemnity.

clue.text: Chop suey not filling — ordered fruitcake

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: not filling says the inner letters of the word suey are dropped, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: Someone orders chop suey but wants it without the filling, a strange request.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not filling' leaves SY from SUEY; with CHOP that gives CHOPSY, which 'ordered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitcake is informal slang for a mad person, and the answer is a colloquial word for a deranged one.

clue.text: One beginning to miss Motor City — America rocks?

indicators.note: to miss means to go without, so a letter is taken out of the city's name

parts.note: Motor City is the nickname of Detroit, home of the US car industry

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the word One

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A visitor sets out to skip Detroit, wondering whether America simply rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing O from DETROIT leaves DETRIT; the question mark marks the definition as an example, rocks being one kind of debris.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is loose debris worn from rock by erosion, so broken rocks are an instance of it.

clue.text: Marketplace investigator with rule, probes French vegetable — judge sporting

parts.note: a square is an open public space where a market is held

indicators.note: probes means goes into, so the detective and rule go inside the vegetable

parts.note: legume is the French word for vegetable
PI is a private investigator

explanation.surface: A market inspector, rule in hand, examines some French produce before giving a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: PIR goes inside LEGUME to make LEGUMPIRE. In cricket, the square leg umpire stands at square leg, level with the batsman, while the other umpire stands behind the stumps.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire is a judge in a game, and this one officiates at cricket from the leg side.

clue.text: Service motor-bikes according to quotation

indicators.note: according to what is quoted, that is spoken, so the word is judged by how it is pronounced

parts.note: Vespas are Italian motor scooters

explanation.surface: A garage services motorbikes, as the quote says.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the scooter name and the church word are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening prayer office of the church, a religious service.

clue.text: See 23
Nurse succeeded avoiding suggestive Spaniard?

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: avoiding means doing without, so one letter is dropped from the racy word

parts.note: risque means suggestive or slightly indecent
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A nurse manages to avoid a Spaniard with a suggestive manner.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a common Spanish man's name, Henry in English, so a Spaniard may bear it; hence the question mark.

clue.text: Stone to massage foot in reflexology

parts.note: to massage is to rub

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot of a word is its last letter, here of reflexology

explanation.surface: A smooth stone is used to massage the foot in reflexology.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is a precious red gemstone, and stone is a common term for a gem.

clue.text: Director avoids trading studio site

indicators.note: avoids says one letter is kept out of the word for trading

parts.note: dealing means trading

explanation.surface: A film director keeps away from business deals at the studio.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a district of west London, home of the famous Ealing film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: The London suburb houses film studios, so it is the location of a studio.

clue.text: Competitive driver who uses gear unconventionally?

definitions.meaning: a motorist who races cars over a short straight track
a racer in drag, someone wearing the gear of the opposite sex

explanation.definitionFit: Drag racing is sprint motor racing, and drag also means cross-dressing clothes, which gives the second reading.

clue.text: Workers around passage act vigilantly

indicators.note: around means the worker insects surround the narrow way

parts.note: worker bees, so bees are workers in crosswords
an alley is a narrow passage

explanation.surface: Workers posted round a passageway keep careful watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To be watching everything closely is to stay alert and vigilant, an idiom for keeping a close lookout.

clue.text: Rugby player's utter position of danger

parts.note: a Lion is a player for the British and Irish Lions rugby team
to mouth is to utter or say

explanation.surface: A rugby player's spoken remark about his place on the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lions are the British and Irish touring rugby union side.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your head in the jaws of the big cat is an idiom for exposing yourself to great peril.

clue.text: Plant, latest in contention, judge brought over

indicators.note: brought over means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, judges a match

indicators.note: latest in picks the final letter of contention

explanation.surface: In a disputed case about a plant, a judge is brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferns are flowerless green plants that reproduce by spores, so the word names a kind of plant.

clue.text: Pen left by American writer

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
US means American

explanation.surface: A pen was left behind by an American author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like the definition, but it is the pig's enclosure; 'writer' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is a pointed implement for writing on wax tablets, so it is a thing that writes.

clue.text: It's flaming stuck underneath footwear … outside wife had a clean

indicators.note: in a down clue stuck underneath places this piece below the previous one
outside says the footwear goes around the abbreviation for wife

parts.note: a shoe is footwear
flaming red, as in a flaming red colour

explanation.surface: Something burning stuck to the bottom of a shoe, so the wife washed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Showered is a past tense verb for washing under a spray, so someone who showered got clean.

clue.text: Sweet ball passed into empty space leads to City's third

indicators.note: passed into says the ball goes inside the remaining letters
empty means the inside of the word space is cleared, keeping its outer letters

parts.note: an orb is a ball or sphere
the third letter of City's is T, and leads to says what comes before it ends the answer

explanation.surface: A football commentary: the ball is passed into space, leading to City's third goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a water ice served as a dessert, a sweet course.

clue.text: Mid-career, one enters into affair — is this what bored secretaries do?

definitions.text: is this what bored secretaries do?

indicators.note: mid takes the central letters of the word career
enters into says the numeral goes inside the word for a fling

parts.note: a fling is a brief affair
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Halfway through her career a bored secretary starts an affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pun: it suggests office romance, but the answer is the dull task of putting papers back in the files.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting documents back into a filing cabinet is routine office work that a secretary does again.

clue.text: American, alienating core of fans, negotiated a share of Albion?

indicators.note: negotiated means worked out or arranged, so the remaining letters are rearranged
alienating means sending away, so some letters are removed
core of takes the middle letters of fans

explanation.surface: An American, losing the support of his fans, has bargained for a stake in Albion football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking AN (the middle of FANS) from AMERICAN leaves AMERIC, which 'negotiated' rearranges. Albion is an old name for Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This was one of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of England, covering the Midlands, a part of Britain.

clue.text: See 11
Two small men, loaded, given a hand in casino

parts.note: Roy is a short man's name
Al is a short man's name
loaded means rich, which is flush

explanation.surface: Two little men with lots of money are dealt a hand at the casino.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, the best possible hand is ace to ten of a single suit.

clue.text: Reflected ages to grasp crossword setter where 'penny' often drops

indicators.note: reflected means mirrored, so the assembled letters are read backwards
to grasp means to hold, so the setter goes inside the word for ages

parts.note: an era is a long age
Dac is the pseudonym of a regular Independent crossword setter

explanation.surface: A long-time puzzle setter muses on the moment when the penny finally drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grasp' makes EDACRA before 'Reflected' turns it. Dac was a long-serving Independent setter, a name solvers of other papers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Penny slot machines at seaside amusement halls take coins dropped into them, hence a penny amusement hall.

clue.text: Become breathless, bunged up, through greeting lady — from Cologne?

indicators.note: through says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: hi is a greeting

indicators.note: in a down clue bunged up means placed going upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: to die is to stop breathing

explanation.surface: Someone gets breathless and blocked up after greeting a woman wearing eau de Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunged up' is the reversal, upwards in a down clue; 'through' is the container. Cologne is a German city, which makes the lady German.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a German girl's name, so a lady from a German city might bear it; the question mark covers the example.

clue.text: Man across pond writing up diary about an aquatic bird

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top
about means around, so the record book surrounds the bird

parts.note: a log is a diary or record
an gives the single letter A
a diver is a water bird, also called a loon

explanation.surface: An American man writes up his diary about a water bird by the pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes LADIVEROG and 'up' reverses it, as a down clue reads upwards. 'Across the pond' is the idiom for across the Atlantic, so in America.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a celebrated American novelist and essayist, so he was a man doing his writing across the Atlantic.

clue.text: Antique business includes forger of cutlery?

indicators.note: includes means the company abbreviation holds the name inside it

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
Uri Geller is famous for bending spoons, so humorously a shaper of cutlery

explanation.surface: An antiques business employs a craftsman who forges knives and forks.
explanation.walkthrough: Uri Geller is the entertainer known for apparently bending spoons by mind power.
explanation.definitionFit: A curio is a rare or unusual collectable object, often an antique piece.

clue.text: Prompt retiring Prince, in Italy, to replant trees

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cue is a prompt

indicators.note: replant means plant again in new places, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A retiring prince in Italy is urged to plant trees again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' turns CUE into EUC; 'to replant' rearranges P plus ITALY into ALYPTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Eucalypts are Australian gum trees, and this Latin plural names several of them.

clue.text: Novelist with no name on grave

indicators.note: with no means lacking, so one letter is taken away

parts.note: Jane Austen is a novelist
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A novelist whose name is missing from the headstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like the noun for a burial place, but it is the adjective for serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave as an adjective means serious and solemn, close to severe in manner.

clue.text: Study annual return, source of income including money from abroad

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room for work
AR is the abbreviation for an annual return, a yearly company filing

indicators.note: source of picks the first letter of both following words

explanation.surface: Someone studies a company's yearly filing and finds foreign currency among its sources of income.
explanation.definitionFit: Denarii were silver coins of ancient Rome, currency from a foreign land.
